source.title: A Loss Curvature Perspective on Training Instability in Deep Learning
source.authors: J. Gilmer; B. Ghorbani; Ankush Garg; Sneha Kudugunta; Behnam Neyshabur; David E. Cardoze; G. Dahl; Zachary Nado; O. Firat

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies learning rates, initialization, warmup, and normalization, then measures curvature and training outcomes. It conceptually tests parts of V1, V4, V5, and V6, though it does not reproduce their full stated settings.
record.gate_note: The paper cites other studies' results for MetaInit, GradInit, and Fixup; those cited comparisons are not extracted as this study's results. The paper's own Table 2 warmup results and its own training experiments are included where they bear on claim versions. Figure-only comparisons are recorded without inferred values.
record.test_reason: The study directly measures curvature, loss and divergence under minibatch training, bearing on V5, and compares learning-rate tolerance with and without BatchNorm, bearing on V6. Training loss does not establish V1's training classification error, and the initialization experiments do not test V4's activation-matched initialization or plain-network depth claims.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. More precisely, successful training avoids or escapes high-curvature regions; initialization, normalization, warmup and clipping can enable higher learning rates through this mechanism. Warmup can match selected specialized-initialization results, sometimes requiring clipping or initialization rescaling. Initial curvature alone does not predict stability, and the study does not establish that initialization has no lasting effect on the broader Hessian spectrum.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures curvature and training stability across varied minibatch learning rates, initialization, warmup, and normalization recipes; it does not reproduce the full recipes in the versions. Its primary optimizer is SGD with momentum, with brief Adam experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome varies with architecture, BatchNorm, initialization, learning rate, warmup length, optimizer, and batch size.

fits_no_version.finding: MetaInit and warmup enable stable training of non-BN residual networks, and initialization's effect on maximum curvature largely disappears after early training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization and warmup can improve early training stability, while later maximum curvature depends strongly on learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Adam training instabilities coincide with crossing an empirical preconditioned-Hessian threshold of 40/η.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive-optimizer instability can track preconditioned curvature under an optimizer-specific empirical threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: Normalization-free ResNet-50 achieves 76.2% ImageNet test accuracy using warmup and gradient clipping.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Warmup and clipping can yield competitive test performance without normalization or specialized initialization.

record.problems: Many key comparisons are figures without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. Some Table 2 comparator values are taken from cited original works rather than the authors' runs. The paper notes that the Adam analysis is brief and leaves deeper analysis for future work.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were left out. Cited results from prior work in Tables 1 and 2 were not extracted as this paper's own experimental outcomes.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error, including random or corrupted labels, is not measured. Loss under MixUp and test accuracy do not establish it.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and the effect of one or two extra neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation in plain networks and its prevention by identity shortcuts; the specified deep plain-network and Fixup alternatives.
Activation-matched signal and gradient preservation, learning speed and trainable depth in plain networks, orthogonal versus Gaussian tanh initialization, and 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
The original wide-network squared-loss setting and full-batch long-run edge-of-stability behavior. The study instead measures related dynamics under minibatch training, mainly with momentum.
The original MNIST, VGG and Inception settings and a controlled replication of Fixup's speed and stability comparison.

missing.what: DenseNet catapult runs: loss initially rises and then normal training resumes despite initial curvature above the threshold.
missing.locator: Section 4; Figure 2 caption and DenseNet catapult markers

missing.what: Successful MetaInit WideResnet training at .1 exhibits progressive sharpening followed by curvature fluctuating around 2/η; distinguish it from the divergent MetaInit run.
Pre- and post-LayerNorm Transformers also become unstable despite starting below the threshold; the record captures only the WideResnet example.
Separate pooled DenseNet comparisons: some BN models have smaller divergence thresholds without warmup; with warmup BN models train above .1 whereas non-BN variants diverge.

Steps to 85% validation accuracy and optimal learning rate across batch sizes for BN and non-BN WideResnets; BN exhibits nearly linear batch-size scaling, while the scaled-initialization non-BN model gains little.
Batch-size dependence of curvature relative to 2/η: batch size 32 remains substantially below the approximation, while 2048 approaches it.

record.verdict_notes: This study is an original source for V5, so no V5 verdict labels are issued. Its minibatch catapult and sharpening observations extend the investigated settings without constituting replications of the squared-loss or full-batch clauses. V1 and V4 labels in the record should be removed.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, Adam, smaller models, early stopping, and regularized recipes are not tested. CIFAR-10 results are primarily described through training loss figures and divergence, not exact training classification error.
The study does not test activation-matched initialization in general, very deep tanh networks, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, or 10,000-layer convolutional networks.

The study does not test the full-batch squared-loss setting or Cohen et al.'s long-run sharpness behavior. Its main experiments use minibatch SGD with momentum; Adam evidence is brief and uses a different empirical threshold.

The study does not test sigmoid networks on MNIST, VGG on CIFAR-10, or Inception on ImageNet. It does not directly compare training speed for the same network with and without batch normalization across the full stated settings.

rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 with and without batch normalization, with MetaInit, or with learning-rate warmup; final training loss plotted against maximum learning rate.
rows.note: The text states that the no-BatchNorm model diverges for learning rates η > .1. The plot gives no extractable exact training-loss values.
rows.check: Use as the non-BN baseline for R2: adding BN permits larger learning rates. Final training loss under MixUp does not establish near-zero training classification error. No activation-matched initialization comparison tests V4.

rows.note: The text says MetaInit allows training without BatchNorm at learning rate .1, but also reports that a MetaInit-initialized model diverged despite starting below the stated stability threshold.
rows.check: MetaInit's effect on residual-network stability does not measure V4's activation-matched initialization or plain-network trainable depth. Training loss does not establish V1. The successful .1 run and the separate divergent MetaInit run should not be combined into one condition.

rows.check: Warmup-enabled training alone establishes neither V1's training classification error, V4's initialization effect, nor V6's BN comparison or Fixup result.

rows.subject: DenseNet, 121 layers
rows.operation_detail: Compared training curvature and divergence with BatchNorm and without BatchNorm; warmup also varied.
rows.measure: Curvature at initialization and divergence during training
rows.note: The authors state that BatchNorm DenseNets start with higher curvature and are more unstable than their non-BN variants in these experiments; with warmup, BN models train at η > .1.
rows.check: Section 4 reports that some BN DenseNets diverge at smaller learning rates, but does not assign that reversal separately to each depth. Higher initial curvature alone is insufficient. Remove V4 and separate the pooled no-warmup result from the warmup comparison.

rows.subject: WideResnet 28-10
rows.operation_detail: Trained a MetaInit-initialized model without warmup and monitored Hessian maximum eigenvalue and loss.
rows.measure: Training stability and Hessian maximum eigenvalue relative to 2/η
rows.value: Diverged despite starting out in a region where λ1 < 2.0/η; curvature grew early and it diverged before step 100.
rows.note: This is the paper's own example of divergence despite initially being below the threshold.
rows.check: Divergence despite initially satisfying λ1 < 2/η directly measures V5's final clause. The stated learning rate .1 is not established for this divergent run: Figure 3C explicitly describes successful MetaInit training at .1, whereas Figure 3D is a separate run.

source_check.correct: Learning rate for the divergent MetaInit run: not stated in the supplied text. Learning rate .1 belongs to the successful MetaInit run in Figure 3C. The divergent run starts with λ1 < 2/η, then sharpens and diverges.
source_check.locator_found: Section 4, final paragraph; Figure 3 caption, C versus D; Section 5; Appendix B and Figure 13.

rows.subject: WideResnet 28-10
rows.operation_detail: Trained the default-initialization non-BN model without warmup at learning rate .1.
rows.note: A direct instability result, but the paper does not describe it as the brief loss-rise-and-recovery behavior in V5.
rows.check: Divergence within three steps is established, but this row does not specify the initial curvature-to-threshold ratio needed to distinguish moderate overshoot from the larger-rate divergence allowed by V5.

rows.subject: WideResnet 28-10
rows.operation_detail: Trained the same default-initialization non-BN model with linear learning-rate warmup.
rows.measure: Training stability and Hessian maximum eigenvalue
rows.baseline: same configuration without warmup, diverged within 3 steps
rows.value: Successful training; curvature gradually decreases during training.
rows.note: The paper does not report this as a catapult recovery; it attributes successful training to warmup pushing parameters toward a flatter region.
rows.check: Successful warmup with decreasing curvature does not itself measure recovery after an above-threshold loss excursion or the full-batch behavior specified by V5.

rows.subject: 6-layer pre-LayerNorm Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adam and monitored the maximum eigenvalue of the preconditioned Hessian under different warmup lengths.
rows.measure: Preconditioned Hessian maximum eigenvalue and training instability
rows.value: Training instability coincides with crossing 40/η; warmup schedule affects curvature.
rows.note: Different optimizer and empirical threshold from the version's 2/η statement; the authors characterize the evidence as brief and leave deeper analysis for future work.
rows.check: Adam instability at an empirically fitted preconditioned-Hessian threshold is a related construct; it does not establish V5's specified recovery or initially-below-threshold divergence.

rows.subject: Resnet-50
rows.operation_detail: Trained without BatchNorm using Fixup, MetaInit, GradInit, or warmup; reported test accuracy.
rows.note: The table reports test accuracy rather than training classification error; Fixup, MetaInit, and GradInit values are taken from their respective original works, while the warmup result is the authors' run.
rows.check: Split the authors' warmup result from cited Fixup, MetaInit and GradInit results. The own-run result is 76.2% test accuracy with warmup plus gradient clipping, dropout and regularization; it measures neither V1's training error nor V4's initialization claim.
